<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Haohui Zhang<sup id="id1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,2,†</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Keyu Chen<sup id="id2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2,†,‡</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Haocheng Sun<sup id="id3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">3</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Weibo Gu<sup id="id4" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Ruizhi Qiao<sup id="id5" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Xing Sun<sup id="id6" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Bo Jiang<sup id="id7" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,∗</span></sup>
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><sup id="id8" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1</span></sup>Shanghai Jiao Tong University  <sup id="id9" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2</span></sup>Tencent YouTu Lab  <sup id="id10" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">3</span></sup>Xiamen University
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Parallel speculative drafting generates multiple candidates in one backbone pass, but independent token selection can produce inconsistent continuations that shorten the accepted prefix. Existing methods mostly leave conditional decoding to a lightweight module after the backbone, which limits the flow of predecessor information to successors. Our analysis of DFlash shows that early positions already form recoverable predictions in shallow layers, and that accurate adjacent predecessors help successors more when they enter earlier. We therefore propose DSpine, a drafter with causal conditioning injection throughout the backbone: at every layer, gated adjacent injection writes each predecessor’s predicted feature into its successor, so the causal conditioning chain unfolds over network depth while all positions update in parallel. A unified transfer space built from the target model’s output embeddings unifies layer-wise injection with predecessor-conditioned decoding, and layer-wise output-embedding supervision promotes the formation of predicted features in shallow layers. Fused kernels and a transition cache execute both efficiently in parallel within SGLang. Across seven math, code, and chat benchmarks, DSpine achieves the longest acceptance length at both temperatures on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B. At temperature zero on Qwen3-8B, it raises the seven-benchmark mean from DFlash’s 3.77 to 4.82 (+27.8%); in SGLang serving tests, it delivers 23.3% higher throughput than DFlash on average.</p>
  
</div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="p1.1" class="ltx_logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">
      
<div id="p1.p1" class="ltx_para"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.36173v2/fig_tau.svg" id="p1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:457/187;" width="457" height="187"></object>
</div>
      
<figure id="S0.F1" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>Mean acceptance length across seven math, code, and chat benchmarks. DSpine leads all compared parallel drafters on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B at temperatures 0 and 1; the annotations report its margin over the strongest baseline in each setting.</figcaption>
</figure>
    
</div>
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Autoregressive decoding is a major source of latency in large language models. Speculative decoding accelerates it without changing the target model: a lightweight drafter proposes multiple candidates, and the target model verifies them in a single forward pass <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Leviathan et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. Its speedup depends on how many candidates are accepted per round and how cheaply they are drafted. Autoregressive drafters such as EAGLE-3 reuse target-model features to improve predictions but still require one sequential drafting step per draft position <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Inspired by diffusion language modeling, DFlash instead predicts a masked block in parallel within one forward pass conditioned on target context features, so a longer draft adds no sequential drafting steps <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This shift also changes how token dependencies are established. Autoregressive drafting conditions each successor on its already selected predecessors, whereas positions in a parallel draft must form predictions before their predecessors commit to tokens, so individually plausible candidates can be inconsistent when combined. Because the target accepts candidates in prefix order, a single inconsistency truncates the rest of the round’s draft, leaving much of the cheaply drafted block unaccepted. Reducing drafting cost must therefore go hand in hand with establishing effective predecessor conditioning inside parallel computation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Recent work improves token consistency in parallel drafts through lightweight conditioning modules. Inside the draft backbone, DFlash2 mixes adjacent positions through local convolutions, but these blend neighboring hidden states without separating the predecessor’s predictive information from the rest of its state <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">DFlash2 Team, 2026</a>)</cite>. Domino, DSpark, and DFlash2’s path selector instead condition on the predecessor after the backbone to adjust token distributions or candidate selection <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">DFlash2 Team, 2026</a>)</cite>. Conditional decoding in these methods is thus left to a lightweight module after the backbone, which limits the flow of predecessor information to successors. Moreover, the predecessor information these modules pass is confined to the final-layer vocabulary space, so it can neither be combined with in-layer features nor exploit the rich intermediate features formed across the backbone.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Our empirical study yields two key insights. <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(1) Earlier positions form predictions at shallower depth:</span> layer-wise readouts already recover substantial token-predictive information at early positions in shallow layers (<a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(a)), so the prefix could condition successors whose computation is still in progress. <span id="S1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(2) Successor prediction depends on both the content of the adjacent predecessor and when it enters the network:</span> even with correct earlier context, replacing only the adjacent predecessor with its draft prediction sharply lowers successor accuracy, and injecting the same correct predecessor features earlier clearly improves it (<a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(c)).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Guided by these insights, we propose <span id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DSpine</span>, a drafter with causal conditioning injection throughout the backbone. At every layer, a gated adjacent injection module writes each predecessor’s predicted feature into its successor, so that the causal conditioning chain unfolds over network depth while all positions update in parallel. We further build a unified transfer space from the output embeddings of the target model, which unifies layer-wise injection with the information transfer in predecessor-conditioned decoding. We also design layer-wise output-embedding supervision that aligns the predicted features with this space, promoting their formation in shallow layers and reducing their discrepancy from token embeddings. Finally, we introduce a transition cache that precomputes the scores of all adjacent candidate pairs in parallel, turning sequential conditional decoding into parallel computation. Our contributions are:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We identify recoverable shallow prefix predictions and the effect of predecessor-conditioning timing, motivating dependency formation across network depth.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose DSpine, which injects causal conditioning throughout the backbone and links it to predecessor-conditioned decoding through a unified output-embedding space with layer-wise supervision.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We demonstrate that DSpine surpasses baselines trained on the same data in both acceptance length and SGLang throughput: on Qwen3-8B, it raises the mean acceptance length from 3.77 for DFlash to 4.82 (<a href="#S0.F1" title="In Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>), and its SGLang throughput exceeds that of DFlash by 23.3%.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Preliminaries</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Speculative Decoding</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given a confirmed context <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\leq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\leq 0}</annotation></semantics></math>, a drafter proposes <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> candidates <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{x}_{1:M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{x}_{1:M}</annotation></semantics></math>, which the target model verifies in one forward pass <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Leviathan et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. Let <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\mathrm{draft},t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>draft</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{draft},t}</annotation></semantics></math> be the actual proposal distribution given this context and preceding candidates; both it and the target distribution <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> include their respective sampling transformations. Conditional on acceptance of all preceding candidates, candidate <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is accepted with probability</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\min\!\left(1,\frac{p_{t}(\hat{x}_{t})}{q_{\mathrm{draft},t}(\hat{x}_{t})}\right),\qquad p_{t}(v)=p_{\mathrm{target}}(v\mid x_{\leq 0},\hat{x}_{1:t-1})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.653em;" width="1.653em"><mi>min</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>draft</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>target</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min\!\left(1,\frac{p_{t}(\hat{x}_{t})}{q_{\mathrm{draft},t}(\hat{x}_{t})}\right),\qquad p_{t}(v)=p_{\mathrm{target}}(v\mid x_{\leq 0},\hat{x}_{1:t-1}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">At the first rejection, the remaining draft is discarded and a replacement is sampled from the corrected distribution (<a href="#A3.E11" title="In Lossless verification. ‣ Appendix C Experimental Details ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>); if all candidates pass, the target supplies an additional token. Greedy decoding accepts candidates matching the target’s choice under the same prefix.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The average acceptance length <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=\mathbb{E}[N_{\mathrm{acc}}]+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>acc</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=\mathbb{E}[N_{\mathrm{acc}}]+1</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of tokens advanced per round, where <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\mathrm{acc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>acc</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\mathrm{acc}}</annotation></semantics></math> counts consecutively accepted draft tokens and the extra one is the correction or additional target token. For a fixed runtime configuration, ignoring prefill and termination costs, the average time per output token (TPOT) is approximately</p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{TPOT}_{\mathrm{spec}}\approx\frac{T_{\mathrm{draft}}+T_{\mathrm{verify}}}{\tau}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>TPOT</mi><mi>spec</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>draft</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>verify</mi></msub></mrow><mi>τ</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{TPOT}_{\mathrm{spec}}\approx\frac{T_{\mathrm{draft}}+T_{\mathrm{verify}}}{\tau},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{draft}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>draft</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{draft}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{verify}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>verify</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{verify}}</annotation></semantics></math> are mean per-round costs, including sampling and cache management. Later candidates contribute only when the preceding prefix is accepted, and acceptance gains must compensate for added drafting cost.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Parallel Drafting</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DFlash-style parallel drafters process a block of <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M+1</annotation></semantics></math> positions, the known anchor <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> followed by <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> masked candidate positions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. In DFlash, fused target-model features over <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{&lt;0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{&lt;0}</annotation></semantics></math> supply K/V at every layer. The backbone updates all positions in one pass with bidirectional block attention, and the LM head shared with the target produces candidate distributions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">An autoregressive drafter generates each token conditioned on the predecessors it has drafted, whereas a DFlash-style drafter predicts every position from the confirmed context alone, so the block proposal factorizes over positions:</p>
<table id="S2.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="q_{\mathrm{draft}}(\hat{x}_{1:M}\mid x_{\leq 0})=\prod_{t=1}^{M}q_{\mathrm{draft},t}(\hat{x}_{t}\mid x_{\leq 0})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>draft</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></munderover><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>draft</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{draft}}(\hat{x}_{1:M}\mid x_{\leq 0})=\prod_{t=1}^{M}q_{\mathrm{draft},t}(\hat{x}_{t}\mid x_{\leq 0}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Each position thus marginalizes over its possible predecessors instead of conditioning on the one actually drafted, and individually likely tokens can form inconsistent combinations. Because verification accepts candidates in prefix order, such inconsistencies cut the accepted prefix, and acceptance decays rapidly at later positions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section asks whether evolving prefix predictions can condition successor computation in parallel drafting. We first examine when predictive information becomes recoverable and when reliable prefix conditions are most useful, then turn to the immediate predecessor: its contribution beyond earlier history and the timing of its use. We use the frozen official Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16 with greedy Qwen3-8B continuations as the correct tokens; datasets, metrics, and full results are in <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Details of the Conditioning Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.36173v2/figure1.svg" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/154;" width="476" height="154"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>(a) Readout accuracy of each layer, grouped by block position. (b) Gain in consecutive correct tokens when the drafted prefix is replaced by the correct prefix at the filled (orange) layers; top: from one layer onward; bottom: at two layers, moving the earlier one. (c) Gain in successor accuracy when, at the specified layers, the adjacent predecessor’s features come from the correct token rather than its draft prediction (L1–L5: all layers); line color marks whether the history before the predecessor is correct (orange) or drafted (blue).</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Early Predictive Cues and the Timing of Conditioning</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To examine when predictive information emerges, we read out predictions from each layer. Intermediate DFlash states lie outside the input space of the target LM head and cannot be decoded directly, so for each layer we fit, on separate data, an equal-capacity lightweight low-rank projection that maps its frozen states into the space decoded by the frozen LM head. At the same shallow depth, early positions are read out much more accurately than distant ones, while all position groups improve with depth (<a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(a)). Although positions update in parallel, predictive information is not equally available: prefixes already carry recoverable cues while successor predictions are still forming, so prefixes could condition successor computation before selecting their own tokens.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We next examine when more accurate prefix conditions are most useful. With a correct token as the anchor, we fill the preceding prefix with draft predictions or correct tokens, which the target model encodes for DFlash’s existing context pathway. Sustained access to correct-prefix features from an early layer yields a 6.7% relative gain in consecutive correct tokens over the all-draft-prefix baseline, and delaying it reduces the gain (<a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(b), sustained conditioning).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Earlier access, however, also means that more layers receive correct features. To isolate timing, we fix the total number of injection layers and vary only their placement: earlier injection raises the relative gain from 1.2% to 4.3% (<a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(b), timing control). Thus, even at a fixed number of uses, earlier access to reliable conditions improves successor prediction: a reliable prefix is valuable not only for more accurate content but also for timely use as successor representations form.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Adjacent Predecessors Shape Successor Predictions</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next examine how the immediate predecessor affects successor prediction. Keeping the target-encoded earlier history correct, we use the predecessor as the anchor of a new draft block: replacing only the correct predecessor with its draft prediction lowers successor accuracy by 31.8 percentage points on average over three block positions (L1–L5 in <a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(c)). Correct earlier history thus does not fully compensate for an inaccurate predecessor: the adjacent token supplies additional predictive cues for its successor.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The predecessor’s effect also depends on when it enters successor computation. Keeping the draft-predicted anchor, we replace its K/V at selected layers with the same-layer K/V cached from a forward pass with the correct predecessor. With correct earlier history, the same number of injection layers, and the same predecessor K/V at the final layer, earlier injection improves successor accuracy over later injection by 14.8 points on average (<a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(c)), indicating that adjacent conditions affect how successor representations form.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">These two observations are complementary: shallow prefix states already carry recoverable predictive cues, and accurate predecessor features help successors more when supplied earlier. Motivated by this, we explore transmitting predecessor prediction features to successors from shallow layers, letting token dependencies build up progressively through network depth (<a href="#S4" title="4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In parallel drafting, every position predicts before its predecessors commit to tokens, so a successor cannot know which token its predecessor will take (<a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Parallel Drafting ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>). DSpine gives each successor what its immediate predecessor is predicting. The observations in <a href="#S3" title="3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> determine where this information comes from and when it arrives: from the adjacent predecessor, which supplies cues that earlier history cannot replace, and from the first layer on, since shallow prefix states already carry recoverable cues and accurate predecessor features help more when supplied earlier.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a) outlines the resulting forward pass. After every Transformer layer, each position receives the feature its predecessor currently predicts, and a gate decides how much of it to absorb; all positions still update in parallel within a single forward pass. After the final layer, each position proposes its top-<math id="S4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> candidates, and tokens are selected from left to right: once a predecessor’s token is selected, it is written into its successor through the same injection, which yields the successor’s final scores. We describe what is passed (<a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Unified Transfer Space ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>), how it is passed inside the backbone (<a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Adjacent Causal Injection ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>), how the same pathway completes decoding (<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Predecessor-Conditioned Decoding ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>), and how the passed features are supervised and the drafter is trained (<a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Layer-Wise Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sections</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a> and <a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Training ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.36173v2/overview_small.png" id="S4.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/174;" width="476" height="174" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Overview of DSpine. (a) Injection passes predecessor features to successors at every layer (green); after the final layer, transition-cached decoding selects each token conditioned on its selected predecessor (orange). (b) One injection layer: predecessor and successor features jointly gate how much of the predecessor’s message enters the successor’s residual stream; training adds cosine alignment to <math id="S4.F3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> and, with probability <math id="S4.F3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>, substitutes <math id="S4.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{y_{t-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{y_{t-1}}</annotation></semantics></math> for the predecessor feature.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Unified Transfer Space</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Existing parallel drafters pass predecessor information to a successor in two ways: inside the backbone, as hidden states mixed across positions by attention or similar operations; after the backbone, as the selected predecessor token fed to an additional module. The former mixes the predecessor’s prediction with the context it has gathered, leaving the successor to infer which token the predecessor favors; the latter provides a decided token but only after all layers have been computed. DSpine passes the predecessor’s prediction itself from the first layer on, expressed in a space where vectors name tokens.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The target LM head scores token <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{v}^{\top}h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>E</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{v}^{\top}h</annotation></semantics></math>, so its output embeddings naturally encode which token a state predicts. We build the unified transfer space from them: we <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>-normalize the rows of the LM head, apply PCA whitening, keep <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> principal directions, and normalize each row again to obtain a fixed embedding table <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Implementation Details of DSpine ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>); whitening removes the component shared by all tokens, so that directions in <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> distinguish tokens. Two kinds of information enter this space. A predecessor whose token is still undetermined contributes a predicted feature: each layer projects its pre-injection state <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{\ell,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{\ell,t}</annotation></semantics></math>, the output of the <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>-th Transformer layer, to <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{\ell,t}=f_{\ell}(u_{\ell,t})=\sqrt{r}\,\normalize(R_{\ell}u_{\ell,t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>r</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>normalize</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{\ell,t}=f_{\ell}(u_{\ell,t})=\sqrt{r}\,\normalize(R_{\ell}u_{\ell,t})</annotation></semantics></math> without intermediate vocabulary decoding, where <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> is a layer-specific learned projection to <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> dimensions and <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\normalize" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>normalize</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\normalize</annotation></semantics></math> denotes <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> normalization. A known token <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, namely the anchor or a decoded predecessor, enters directly as its embedding <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{r}\,C_{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>r</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{r}\,C_{x}</annotation></semantics></math>. Because both take the same form, a single pathway can carry either a prediction or a decided token: DSpine passes predicted features inside the backbone and decoded tokens in predecessor-conditioned decoding.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Adjacent Causal Injection</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After the <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>-th Transformer layer, position <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> receives a message from its immediate predecessor only. Shallow predecessor features are still forming and vary in reliability, so the successor gates how much of the message to absorb: the receiver feature <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{\ell,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{\ell,t}</annotation></semantics></math> and the predecessor feature <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{\ell,t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{\ell,t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> jointly determine the gate, while the predecessor feature is projected into a message that is gated and written back to the residual stream:</p>
<table id="S4.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E4"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle g_{\ell,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle g_{\ell,t}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\sigma\!\left(G_{q}z_{\ell,t}+G_{p}z_{\ell,t-1}+b\right)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.437em;" width="0.437em"><mi>σ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sigma\!\left(G_{q}z_{\ell,t}+G_{p}z_{\ell,t-1}+b\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<tbody id="S4.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle m_{\ell,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle m_{\ell,t}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=Az_{\ell,t-1}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=Az_{\ell,t-1},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
