</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is the sigmoid function; <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{q}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> are shared across layers, and each layer has its own write matrix <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. All messages use pre-update features, so injection within a layer runs in parallel across positions; the anchor remains unchanged.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Block-causal attention.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike DFlash and other parallel drafters with bidirectional block attention, DSpine uses block-causal attention in all <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> backbone layers: position <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> attends only to target-context K/V and block positions <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0,\ldots,t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0,\ldots,t</annotation></semantics></math>. Attention and injection thus share the predecessor-to-successor direction, and the correct information injected into a position during training cannot flow back to earlier positions (<a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Training ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>). Drafting remains a single, block-parallel forward pass.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Propagation through depth.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because earlier access to accurate predecessor features benefits successor prediction (<a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(c)), injection starts at the first layer and its effects propagate through depth: messages received at one layer enter the next layer’s computation, shaping the predicted features that successors send onward. For example, information that <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t-1</annotation></semantics></math> receives from <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t-2</annotation></semantics></math> at layer <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> can influence the message sent to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> at layer <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell+1</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>(a)). The causal conditioning chain thus unfolds over network depth while positions within each layer update in parallel; earlier context remains accessible through block-causal attention.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fused layer-wise injection.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Layer-wise injection consists of small normalization, projection, gating, and residual-write operations, which a direct implementation executes as many kernel launches with intermediate tensor traffic. We merge the three projections into one matrix multiplication and use two fused kernels, one for the gated message and one for the residual write together with the next layer’s input normalization, all executed within the draft backbone’s CUDA graph.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Predecessor-Conditioned Decoding</h3>

<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_floatright" style="width:44%;"><img src="2609.36173v2/transition_cache.png" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:215/186;" width="215" height="186" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span>Transition cache. (a) Serial conditional scoring. (b) Parallel transition precomputation followed by sequential selection; greedy implementation shown.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Predecessor-conditioned decoding conditions each position on the token actually decoded at its predecessor, rather than on its predicted feature, and it needs no new module. The final-layer output <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{L,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{L,t}</annotation></semantics></math> first passes through the final RMSNorm and shared LM head to determine each position’s initial top-<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> candidates. A decoded predecessor is a known token, so it enters the unified transfer space directly and passes through the same final-layer injection: for a token <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> at position <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t-1</annotation></semantics></math>, we replace the predicted feature <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{L,t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{L,t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{r}\,C_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>r</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{r}\,C_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, changing both gate and message, and redo the final-layer write (<a href="#S4.E5" title="In 4.2 Adjacent Causal Injection ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) from the cached pre-injection state <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{L,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{L,t}</annotation></semantics></math>. We denote the output by <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}^{\mathrm{o}}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}^{\mathrm{o}}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> and call this step <em id="S4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">last-write refinement</em>; the shared LM head maps it to conditional scores <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{t}(s,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t}(s,v)</annotation></semantics></math> over the initial candidates.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Transition-cached decoding.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because each position’s scores depend on the predecessor’s choice, computing them directly proceeds sequentially across positions. The transition cache removes this sequential computation: once the backbone has fixed each position’s pre-injection state <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{L,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{L,t}</annotation></semantics></math> and top-<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> candidate set <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{t}=\{v_{t,1},\ldots,v_{t,K}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{t}=\{v_{t,1},\ldots,v_{t,K}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, last-write refinement depends only on the predecessor’s token, so before selection we compute the refined final-layer features for all predecessor candidates in parallel and score the successor candidates, organized as <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{t}[i,j]=S_{t}(v_{t-1,i},v_{t,j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{t}[i,j]=S_{t}(v_{t-1,i},v_{t,j})</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4.3 Predecessor-Conditioned Decoding ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). Enumerating all <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>K</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> pairs per transition trades additional scoring work for a shorter sequential dependency chain; in practice, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=16</annotation></semantics></math> suffices at a small additional cost (<a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Decoding Latency Breakdown ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a>). Selection then proceeds through the cache from the first position, without any sequential matrix operations.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Layer-Wise Output-Embedding Supervision</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The predicted features that injection passes serve two roles, and the final-layer loss shapes them only indirectly through later computation. First, they condition successors from the first layer on, yet in shallow layers they carry recoverable cues but are still forming (<a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(a)). Second, the injection receives predicted features inside the backbone but token embeddings in predecessor-conditioned decoding, so the two should lie close in the unified transfer space. DSpine therefore aligns the predicted features at every layer directly with the correct token’s embedding, promoting their formation in shallow layers and narrowing their gap to the token embeddings used in predecessor-conditioned decoding.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Directional alignment.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With the projection <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> used for injection, we read <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{\ell,i}=f_{\ell}(h_{\ell,i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{\ell,i}=f_{\ell}(h_{\ell,i})</annotation></semantics></math> from post-injection states and align it with the correct token’s embedding <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{y_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{y_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{emb}}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\sum_{i}w_{i}\left[1-\cos\!\left(e_{\ell,i},C_{y_{i}}\right)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>emb</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.216em;" width="1.216em"><mi>cos</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{emb}}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\sum_{i}w_{i}\left[1-\cos\!\left(e_{\ell,i},C_{y_{i}}\right)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="w_{i}=\exp(-(t_{i}-1)/\gamma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{i}=\exp(-(t_{i}-1)/\gamma)</annotation></semantics></math> is the decay weight for block position <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. Because the readout follows injection, this loss trains both the formation of each feature and the successor’s use of the received message; it constrains only the direction of a low-dimensional projection, leaving the full hidden state free for contextual computation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Training</h3>

<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We sample draft blocks from training sequences and train the drafter with the target model, shared input embeddings, and LM head frozen. Training supervises two outputs. The first is the ordinary final-layer output, which predicts over the full vocabulary and determines the top-<math id="S4.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> candidates. The second is the output of last-write refinement: as at inference, it replaces the predicted predecessor feature with a token embedding and redoes the final-layer write, except that the correct predecessor token is used, and predicts only over those candidates. Both receive the same loss below, jointly training candidate generation and predecessor-conditioned decoding.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S4.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the draft and target distributions at position <math id="S4.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> under the correct prefix. Following the loss design of DSpark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, the loss is a weighted mix of token cross-entropy and probability <math id="S4.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> distance:</p>
<table id="S4.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dist}}=\sum_{i}w_{i}\Bigl[-\alpha\log q_{i}(y_{i})+(1-\alpha)\,\|q_{i}-p_{i}\|_{1}\Bigr]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>dist</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dist}}=\sum_{i}w_{i}\Bigl[-\alpha\log q_{i}(y_{i})+(1-\alpha)\,\|q_{i}-p_{i}\|_{1}\Bigr],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS5.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> is the mixing weight. The output of last-write refinement is also included in <math id="S4.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dist}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>dist</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dist}}</annotation></semantics></math>, except that its distributions are restricted to the top-<math id="S4.SS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> candidates, with the target renormalized to that set.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Early in training, predicted features carry little reliable information, which gives the injection little to learn from. We therefore replace shallow-layer predecessor features with correct-token embeddings with some probability, keeping receiver features model-derived <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bengio et al., 2015</a>)</cite>, and gradually phase this replacement out; the unified transfer space makes this substitution direct. Last-write refinement always uses correct predecessors. The overall training objective weights layer-wise supervision by <math id="S4.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> (coefficients and schedules in <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Implementation Details of DSpine ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>):</p>
<table id="S4.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dist}}+\lambda\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{emb}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>dist</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>emb</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{dist}}+\lambda\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{emb}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Models and evaluations.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct experiments on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> with thinking mode disabled, covering three task categories: <em id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Math</em>: GSM8K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cobbe et al., 2021</a>)</cite> and MATH-500 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lightman et al., 2023</a>)</cite>; <em id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Code</em>: HumanEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, MBPP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Austin et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, and LiveCodeBench (LCB) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jain et al., 2024</a>)</cite>; <em id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Chat</em>: MT-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2023a</a>)</cite> and Arena-Hard <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>. On all seven benchmarks, we measure the average acceptance length <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Speculative Decoding ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>) in SGLang <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2023b</a>)</cite> at temperatures 0 and 1; serving throughput is measured on GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, and MBPP at temperature 0 and concurrency 2–32, with the same fixed verification budget for all methods (<a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Experimental Details ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Baselines.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare with four representative state-of-the-art parallel drafters: DFlash <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, Domino <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, DSpark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, and DFlash2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">DFlash2 Team, 2026</a>)</cite>. DFlash selects tokens independently across positions; the other three build on the DFlash backbone to model intra-block dependencies.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implementation.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each target model, all drafters are retrained on the same ShareGPT data, with responses regenerated by the target; backbones use five layers and a block size of 16 and are trained for six epochs with the same global batch size and learning-rate schedule (<a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Implementation Details of DSpine ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<td id="S5.T1.2.1.12.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.6pt 3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.2.1.12.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBEEE3;">4.29<span id="S5.T1.2.1.12.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> / </span>3.79</span></td>
<td id="S5.T1.2.1.12.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.6pt 3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.2.1.12.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBEEE3;">4.19<span id="S5.T1.2.1.12.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> / </span>3.84</span></td>
<td id="S5.T1.2.1.12.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.6pt 3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.2.1.12.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBEEE3;">4.02<span id="S5.T1.2.1.12.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> / </span>3.64</span></td>
<td id="S5.T1.2.1.12.10" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.6pt 3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.2.1.12.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBEEE3;">4.75<span id="S5.T1.2.1.12.10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> / </span>4.38</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#S5.T1" title="In 5.2 Main Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, DSpine achieves the longest acceptance length on all benchmarks for both models at both temperatures. On Qwen3-8B, it raises the average <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> of DFlash from 3.77 to 4.82 and leads the strongest baseline by 10.0% with greedy decoding (DFlash2) and by 12.8% under sampling (DSpark); on Qwen3-4B, its lead over the strongest baseline, DFlash2, is 5.4% and 10.1%, respectively. Domino, DSpark, and DFlash2, which condition on predecessors after the backbone, already improve substantially over DFlash, while DSpine, which conditions on predecessors at every layer and again at token selection, extends the gain further, with a larger lead under sampling (see <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Experimental Details ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a> for each method’s proposal policy at temperature one).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Serving Throughput</h3>

<figure id="S5.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.36173v2/sglang_throughput.svg" id="S5.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/182;" width="476" height="182"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>Serving throughput gain over DFlash on SGLang, in thousands of tokens per second (temperature zero). The dashed zero line is DFlash; shading and the strip above each panel give the lead of DSpine over DFlash2, the strongest baseline.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#S5.F5" title="In 5.3 Serving Throughput ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, DSpine achieves the highest throughput at every task and concurrency level on both models: on Qwen3-8B it outperforms the strongest baseline, DFlash2, by 11.1% on average and reaches up to 4.0<math id="S5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> speedup over autoregressive decoding (<a href="#A3.T8" title="In Appendix C Experimental Details ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>); on Qwen3-4B it leads DFlash2 by 6.5% on average. The gain in acceptance length thus carries over to serving, and the extra cost of layer-wise injection and transition-cached decoding (<a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Decoding Latency Breakdown ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a>) does not offset it.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4 </span>Decoding Latency Breakdown</h3>

<figure id="S5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.36173v2/latency_breakdown.svg" id="S5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/110;" width="476" height="110"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>Module-level breakdown of Qwen3-8B decoding time on SGLang.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To examine where decoding time goes, we time each decoding round of Qwen3-8B in SGLang, split into a draft stage and a verification stage. As shown in <a href="#S5.F6" title="In 5.4 Decoding Latency Breakdown ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, verification takes 72–76% of round time and costs about the same for all methods. DSpine’s parallel injection adds at most 0.15 ms per round across all five layers, and its predecessor-conditioned decoding, which scores candidates and selects through the transition cache (<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Predecessor-Conditioned Decoding ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>), costs less than half as much as the post-backbone heads of DSpark and Domino. Overall, a DSpine round costs about as much as a DFlash2 round (7.14 vs. 7.19 ms), and because more tokens are accepted per round, DSpine spends 10.9% less decoding time per generated token than DFlash2.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Effect of each component.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train each variant in <a href="#S5.T3" title="In 5.5 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> independently. Removing last-write refinement reduces <math id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> by 6.6–7.1%, and further removing parallel injection enlarges the drop to 8.8–10.7%. Both components improve acceptance length, and their contributions are complementary.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Supervision target.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S5.T3" title="In 5.5 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> compares intermediate-layer supervision: directional supervision toward compact output embeddings improves acceptance length, whereas per-layer full-vocabulary cross-entropy falls below the unsupervised baseline. This supports the design of <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Layer-Wise Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>, as forcing intermediate states to classify tokens may interfere with later layers’ contextual computation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Speculative decoding lets a lightweight drafter propose tokens that the target model verifies losslessly <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Leviathan et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. Follow-ups mainly improve the drafter: Medusa predicts several positions with independent heads, Hydra makes these heads depend on drafted tokens <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cai et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ankner et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, the EAGLE series drafts autoregressively from target features <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024c</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and tree verification checks multiple continuations per round <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Miao et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024c</a>)</cite>. Autoregressive drafting conditions each token on its predecessors but costs one sequential step per token.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Parallel decoding methods predict multiple positions at once <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stern et al., 2018</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">An et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Christopher et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. DFlash drafts a block in one pass of a lightweight block-diffusion model conditioned on target features <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2026</a>)</cite>; follow-ups add layer-wise target conditioning, position-weighted losses, or draft trees <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ringel and Romano, 2026</a>)</cite>. Since positions predict before their predecessors commit, the resulting tokens can be inconsistent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stern et al., 2018</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. Most remedies restore this dependency after the backbone, through a causal correction branch (Domino), a sequential head (DSpark), or a path selector over top-<math id="S6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> candidates (DFlash2) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">DFlash2 Team, 2026</a>)</cite>, as well as previous-token conditioning, block refinement, or adjacent-candidate scoring <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rheinboldt et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rusanovsky et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. Inside the backbone, DFlash2 adds causal two-tap convolutions, and DART and JetSpec use causal block attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">DFlash2 Team, 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. DSpine also uses block-causal attention but additionally injects each predecessor’s predicted feature, supervised in a unified transfer space, into its successor at every layer; the same injection carries decoded tokens in predecessor-conditioned decoding.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DSpine injects causal conditioning throughout the backbone, building intra-block token dependencies over network depth within a single parallel drafting pass. Gated adjacent injection passes predecessor features to successors at every layer, and a unified transfer space with layer-wise supervision links this injection to predecessor-conditioned decoding. A transition cache precomputes the scores of all adjacent candidate pairs in parallel, turning sequential conditional decoding into parallel computation. Across math, code, and chat tasks, DSpine improves acceptance length over representative parallel drafters and translates these gains into higher SGLang serving throughput. These results motivate further study of in-layer information transfer, including more flexible communication ranges and interactions in other parallel decoding architectures.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Implementation Details of DSpine</h2>

<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Architecture.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DSpine builds on the DFlash drafter for Qwen3-8B (<a href="#A1.T4" title="In Training setup. ‣ Appendix A Implementation Details of DSpine ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>): five Transformer layers with block-causal attention, target context features fused from five target layers and supplied as K/V to every layer, and the target’s input embedding and LM head shared and frozen. Injection adds about 33M parameters, roughly 3% of the backbone.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Unified transfer space.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{E}_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{E}_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> be the <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>-normalized LM-head row of token <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> its mean over the vocabulary, and let <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> hold the top <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the centered Gram matrix <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{v}(\bar{E}_{v}-\mu)(\bar{E}_{v}-\mu)^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>v</mi></msub><mrow><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{v}(\bar{E}_{v}-\mu)(\bar{E}_{v}-\mu)^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>. The table is <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="C_{v}=\normalize\bigl(\Lambda_{r}^{-1/2}P_{r}^{\top}(\bar{E}_{v}-\mu)\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>normalize</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>E</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{v}=\normalize\bigl(\Lambda_{r}^{-1/2}P_{r}^{\top}(\bar{E}_{v}-\mu)\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math>, fixed and shared by all layers.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Initialization.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each readout matrix <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> is initialized with <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{r}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{r}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>; the write matrices <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and the predecessor gate matrix <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> are zero-initialized with <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b=0</annotation></semantics></math>, so every injection starts as the identity map.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Losses.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both the backbone output and the last-write refinement output use <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.1</annotation></semantics></math> in <a href="#S4.E7" title="In 4.5 Training ‣ 4 DSpine: Adjacent Causal Injection and Output-Embedding Supervision ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> and are summed with equal weight. The layer-wise supervision weight is <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=\beta_{t}\,\sg(\mathrm{CE}_{\mathrm{bb}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>sg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>CE</mi><mi>bb</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=\beta_{t}\,\sg(\mathrm{CE}_{\mathrm{bb}})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CE}_{\mathrm{bb}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>CE</mi><mi>bb</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CE}_{\mathrm{bb}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the token cross-entropy of the backbone output and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> rises linearly from 0 to 0.5 over the first 146 steps. For last-write refinement, the cross-entropy term is computed only where the correct token lies among the <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=16</annotation></semantics></math> candidates, and the <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> term only where the candidates hold more than <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> of the target probability, against the target distribution renormalized to the candidates.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Correct-predecessor curriculum.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each draft block is selected with probability <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> by one draw shared by layers 1–3, which then use <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{r}\,C_{y_{t-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>r</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{r}\,C_{y_{t-1}}</annotation></semantics></math> as predecessor input. <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> for the first sixth of training and decays linearly to zero at one third.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training setup.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All drafters share the same training configuration: the same ShareGPT data with responses regenerated by the target model with thinking disabled, the same draft block of one anchor and 15 candidates, a global batch of 112 sequences, AdamW without weight decay at a peak learning rate of <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> with 4% linear warmup (146 steps) and cosine decay to zero, a maximum training sequence length of 3,072 tokens, and six epochs (3,655 steps). <a href="#A1.T4" title="In Training setup. ‣ Appendix A Implementation Details of DSpine ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> lists the remaining DSpine hyperparameters.</p>
</div>

<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Details of the Conditioning Experiments</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Setup, Readouts, and Metrics</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the GSM8K test set and HumanEval with the frozen official Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16 drafter; greedy Qwen3-8B continuations (thinking disabled, at most 1,024 new tokens) serve as correct tokens. Each block contains one anchor and 15 candidates.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For layer <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, the readout is</p>
<table id="A2.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\ell}=\softmax\!\left(E[n(h_{\ell})+U_{\ell}V_{\ell}n(h_{\ell})+b_{\ell}]\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mi>softmax</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\ell}=\softmax\!\left(E[n(h_{\ell})+U_{\ell}V_{\ell}n(h_{\ell})+b_{\ell}]\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> is the frozen target LM head, <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> is RMS normalization without a trainable scale, and <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\ell}V_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\ell}V_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> has rank 64. Each readout is fitted with cross-entropy on 500 GSM8K training questions and selected on another 100, both disjoint from the test data (AdamW, three epochs, batch size 256, learning rate <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>, weight decay <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, 5% warmup, cosine decay).</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> evaluated positions, the number of consecutive correct tokens is</p>
<table id="A2.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E10.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="K_{T}=\sum_{j=1}^{T}\prod_{t=1}^{j}\mathbb{I}[\hat{y}_{t}=y_{t}]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>j</mi></munderover><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{T}=\sum_{j=1}^{T}\prod_{t=1}^{j}\mathbb{I}[\hat{y}_{t}=y_{t}],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">which, unlike <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, compares predictions with fixed correct continuations. We average blocks within each task and then over tasks; panels (b) and (c) of <a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> average GSM8K and HumanEval with equal weight.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Prefix Content and Timing</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We fix the correct token <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{7}</annotation></semantics></math> as a new anchor and fill <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1},\ldots,x_{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1},\ldots,x_{6}</annotation></semantics></math> with either draft predictions (P) or correct tokens (G), keeping earlier context unchanged. The target model encodes the context up to <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, and its fused features enter each draft layer as K/V; layer 1 always receives P features, while layers 2–5 follow the chosen schedule. We evaluate <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{8},\ldots,x_{15}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>15</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{8},\ldots,x_{15}</annotation></semantics></math> and report the relative gain in <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>K</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{8}</annotation></semantics></math> over the all-P schedule. <a href="#A2.T5" title="In B.2 Prefix Content and Timing ‣ Appendix B Details of the Conditioning Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> lists all schedules, and <a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(b) shows the average of the two datasets.</p>
</div>

<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Adjacent Predecessor versus Earlier History</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For original-block positions 4, 8, and 12, we use the immediately preceding token as a new anchor; the earlier history and the anchor independently take draft predictions or correct tokens. The history is encoded by the target model and the predecessor enters the drafter through its input embedding, so each evaluated token is the first candidate of its new block. <a href="#A2.T6" title="In B.3 Adjacent Predecessor versus Earlier History ‣ Appendix B Details of the Conditioning Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> reports the gain from correcting only the predecessor; the L1–L5 points in <a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(c) average it over the three positions. Correcting the predecessor helps in every setting; at position 12 with correct history, accuracy rises from 51.00% to 93.50% on GSM8K and from 48.78% to 91.31% on HumanEval.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T6" class="ltx_table">

<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Timing of Predecessor Features</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We cache the predecessor’s K/V at every layer in two forward passes, one with the predicted and one with the correct predecessor, and substitute the correct K/V only at selected layers. The comparison supplies correct features twice: at layer 5 and at one of layers 2–4. The all-predicted and all-correct schedules reproduce the two native forward passes, so the L1–L5 points in <a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 When and How Prefix Predictions Condition Parallel Drafting ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(c) equal the content effect in <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Adjacent Predecessor versus Earlier History ‣ Appendix B Details of the Conditioning Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>. Averaged over the three positions, L2+L5 improves accuracy over L4+L5 by 14.33 and 15.24 points on GSM8K and HumanEval with correct history (<a href="#A2.T7" title="In B.4 Timing of Predecessor Features ‣ Appendix B Details of the Conditioning Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>), and by 9.63 and 8.99 points with predicted history.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span>L2+L5 minus L4+L5 with correct earlier history. </figure>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each benchmark uses its complete test set (1,319 GSM8K, 500 MATH-500, 164 HumanEval, 500 MBPP, 1,055 LCB, 80 MT-Bench, and 500 Arena-Hard prompts; MT-Bench runs both turns). All methods receive identical prompts without a system message and generate at most 2,048 new tokens. Acceptance length in <a href="#S5.T1" title="In 5.2 Main Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> is measured in SGLang with eight single-GPU instances, each serving up to 16 concurrent requests; at temperature one, tokens are sampled from the full target distribution. Every method proposes 15 draft tokens per round. <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is averaged over the responses of each benchmark, and Avg. is the unweighted mean over benchmarks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Lossless verification.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the first rejection occurs at position <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, we keep <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{x}_{1:j-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{x}_{1:j-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and sample a replacement from</p>
<table id="A3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math> is the vocabulary; if all <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> candidates are accepted, one additional token is sampled from the target. Together with <a href="#S2.E1" title="In 2.1 Speculative Decoding ‣ 2 Preliminaries ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, this preserves the target distribution.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoding at temperature one.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All methods use SGLang’s lossless verification. DSpark, DFlash2, and DSpine sample their proposals, the latter two from the softmax of their selector or transition-cache scores over the top-16 candidates of each position, and apply rejection sampling with these proposal probabilities; DFlash and Domino propose greedily and accept a candidate when it matches the token sampled from the target.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Serving.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each instance uses one GPU (tensor parallelism one, BF16, FlashAttention-3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shah et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, CUDA graphs) at temperature zero with at most 2,048 output tokens on the complete GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, and MBPP test sets, with identical prompts in the same order. Throughput is the total number of output tokens divided by the wall-clock time of the whole workload, including prefill and scheduling. All methods use the same static budget of 15 draft tokens per round.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Supervision targets.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The variants in <a href="#S5.T3" title="In 5.5 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> use the same training data, disable injection, and are trained for three epochs (1,827 steps); token CE decodes every layer through the shared final RMSNorm and the frozen target LM head. All variants are evaluated in SGLang at temperature zero.</p>
</div>
</section>

              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
